entry.title: Why Optimistic UI Updates Are Corrosive to User Trust
entry.content:
Links: datastar-instant-intent.ndyg.cross.stream | lobsters

Optimistic UI updates normalize software that deceives users by displaying unverified states before server confirmation. When actions like liking a post or flipping a switch appear successful immediately but fail silently in the background, it erodes trust and requires complex reconciliation machinery to manage desynchronization.

Avoiding optimistic updates ensures that software communicates known truths to users while simplifying development by letting the backend act as the single source of truth. Using tools like Datastar, developers can display precise client-side feedback—such as loading states and blinking indicators—without lying about whether a request has actually succeeded.

The environment provides comprehensive functionality including Wayland surfaces for graphical interfaces, Mesa-based 3D rendering via WebGL2, and ALSA audio support. It also supports networking for tools like curl, git, and pip through Wisp relays. By facilitating complex operations such as nested browser instances, trynix.dev demonstrates the practical application of Atwood’s Law, where any application capable of being written in JavaScript eventually becomes a web-based reality.

entry.content:

Iris Meredith argues that a lack of reading habits among software engineers correlates with a deficiency in curiosity, which compromises their ability to make responsible decisions in positions of technical power. She frames programming as a primary form of written communication, asserting that the readability and logical structure of a codebase are as critical to its utility as its machine execution. Consequently, developers who do not engage with literature often produce unmaintainable code and struggle to understand the human needs behind the software they build.

Meredith distinguishes software engineering from manual trades by noting that developers often influence significant societal outcomes, such as financial access and user experience. She suggests that engineers who are well-read are better equipped to empathize with their audience and communicate complex ideas clearly. The essay advocates for a cultural shift within the tech industry to value literary literacy as a necessary skill for producing high-quality, socially responsible software.

entry.title: CLI Tools Combined to Find Geographic Midpoints on macOS
entry.content:
Links: george.mand.is | lobsters | hacker news

George Mandis describes a workflow using three command-line tools—whereami, nearme, and jq—to identify locations halfway between two geographic points. By piping the JSON output of whereami (a geolocation and reverse geocoding tool) into jq for coordinate averaging, and then into nearme (which utilizes Apple's MapKit), users can search for nearby venues at the midpoint without requiring API keys or a web browser.

The method is restricted to macOS due to its reliance on native geocoding and MapKit frameworks. While the geographic average calculation is a literal midpoint that does not account for real-world factors like travel time or traffic, the author provides shell functions for both Zsh and Fish to simplify the complex command-line piping into a single command for finding places like coffee shops or bars.

entry.title: AFK-surf Releases Xnulinux to Run macOS Kernel as a Linux Kernel Module
entry.content:
Links: github.com | hacker news

Xnulinux is a project that builds Apple's open-source XNU kernel and runs it as a loadable kernel module inside an unmodified arm64 Linux kernel. By allowing XNU to drive the CPU and memory directly via a foreign kernel interface module, macOS userspace applications run natively alongside Linux processes without a traditional hypervisor.

Running on an Apple Silicon Mac within an arm64 Linux virtual machine, the system boots a macOS system disk to a functional desktop environment with working applications, networking, and GPU acceleration. The repository separates components by license, utilizing an APSL-2.0 kernel module for XNU and a GPL-2.0 interface module for Linux integration.
